newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Estonian premier happy at EU talks agreement.
newsitem.headline: Estonian premier happy at EU talks agreement.

text.p: Estonian Prime Minister Mart Siiman welcomed a European Commission agreement on Thursday to recommend the European Union open membership talks with Estonia and five other countries.

"Fine," was his first reaction as he broke into a broad smile and shook hands with other members of the Estonian delegation at the second Central and Eastern European Economic Sunmmit in the Austrian city of Salzburg.
"We are extremely happy about this and our expectations are getting into reality," Siiman told Reuters, speaking through an interpreter.

"At the same time, we know we are not in the European Union. We have just got a very good acknowledgement and we know we have to do everything possible to go through the negotiations and get into the real accession process."
The Commission agreed in principle to recommend the EU open accession talks with Poland, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovenia, Estonia and Cyprus.

The economy in Estonia, a tiny Baltic republic formerly part of the old Soviet Union, grew sharply in the last two quarters of 1996 and the government has forecast GDP will rise 4-5 percent this year.

Siiman earlier told a summit plenary session on priorities for the region that Estonia could not adopt just an Anglo-Saxon or European model but had to have its own, tailored to the needs of the country.
"It is the model which has now brought us to the point where we are now ready to start accession negotiations with the EU," he said.
